about: Green Asia Impex sources, processes and exports frozen shrimps and dried chillies to B2B customers (importers, distributors, food processors) in India and abroad. It runs a shrimp processing plant at Unguturu, Tadepalligudem, Andhra Pradesh (10,800 MTPA installed) and is a Two Star Export House. Shrimps are 87.76% of FY26 revenue from operations of about Rs 383.80 crore; it exports to China, Kuwait, USA, Malaysia, UK, Vietnam and Thailand.
sector: Seafood processing and agri-commodity exports (frozen shrimp, dried chillies)

objects.purpose: Capital expenditure for setting up proposed seafood processing facility at Chinnayagudem (plant, machinery and equipment); total project cost Rs 51.27 crore, of which Rs 40.03 crore from Net Proceeds and balance from internal accruals
General corporate purposes (capped at lower of 15% of gross proceeds or Rs 10 crore)

promoters.background: Venkata Ramarao (age 52) is Managing Director; Meenakshi is the co-promoter. Both are Promoter Selling Shareholders in the Rs 7.00 crore OFS (Rs 3.70 crore and Rs 3.30 crore).

concentration.note: Top ten customers in each of the two segments together were 77.85% of FY26 revenue from operations (69.52% in FY25). Shrimp top-5 customers were 58.10% of shrimp revenue and dried-chilli top-5 were 80.61%. China customers were 31.29% of FY26 revenue.

litigation_note: Contingent liability of Rs 7.89 crore (19.04% of net worth) is an income tax demand for FY2021-22 under appeal; Rs 0.54 crore deposited under protest and balance pre-deposit installments pending. Four tax proceedings are outstanding against the company; no other material litigation disclosed.
strengths: Export-oriented shrimp processing plant with HACCP, ISO 22000, FDA and GACC approvals, and recognised as a Two Star Export House.
Revenue grew from Rs 317 crore in FY24 to Rs 384 crore in FY26, and PAT more than doubled from Rs 6.66 crore to Rs 15.61 crore.
Margins are improving: PAT margin rose from 2.10% to 4.07% and EBITDA margin from 5.47% to 6.57% over FY24-FY26.
Return ratios are high, with ROE of 46.43% and ROCE of 19.69% in FY26, though helped by a heavily borrowed balance sheet.
Leverage is falling: debt-to-equity improved from 4.12x in FY24 to 2.40x in FY26.
Two product lines (shrimp and dried chillies) with different seasonal peaks help spread procurement and processing across the year.
About 74% of FY26 revenue came from repeat customers, and the company ships to seven countries.
Planned new Chinnayagudem facility would roughly double installed capacity from 10,800 to 21,900 MTPA, with value-added IQF and ready-to-cook products.

risks.title: High customer concentration
risks.detail: Top ten customers in the two segments made up 77.85% of FY26 revenue (69.52% in FY25); dried-chilli top five were 80.61% of that segment. Business is B2B with no long-term contracts.

risks.title: Heavy debt and working capital dependence
risks.detail: Borrowings were Rs 99.47 crore at March 2026 against net worth of Rs 41.43 crore (debt/equity 2.40x). Financing agreements carry restrictive covenants and the business needs large working capital.

risks.title: Negative operating cash flow
risks.detail: Operating cash flow was negative in all three years: -Rs 15.00 crore (FY24), -Rs 5.06 crore (FY25) and -Rs 6.27 crore (FY26), funded by borrowings.

risks.title: Dependence on China and on shrimp
risks.detail: Sales to China were 31.29% of FY26 revenue (Rs 120.09 crore), and shrimps were 87.76% of revenue, so any China or shrimp-sector shock would hit hard.

risks.title: Income tax demand and contingent liabilities
risks.detail: Contingent liability of Rs 7.89 crore (19.04% of net worth) for an FY2021-22 income tax demand under appeal; the company has asked for more time to pay the balance pre-deposit citing cash flow constraints.

risks.title: Thin margins and no hedging policy
risks.detail: PAT margin is only 4.07% and EBITDA margin 6.57%. The company has no formal foreign exchange hedging policy despite export sales and foreign currency payables.

risks.title: Expansion project not yet ordered
risks.detail: Rs 40.03 crore of net proceeds goes to a new plant, but machinery orders are not yet placed, risking delay and cost overruns. Commercial operations are expected only in FY2029. Existing block-freezing utilisation is only about 55%.

risks.title: Compliance lapses and related-party dealings
risks.detail: Many statutory filings were delayed, some by hundreds of days, and manufacturing began before the object clause was added to the MOA (Sept 2025). Related-party dealings exist, including a Rs 2.75 crore advance to promoter-linked Green Asia Corp.
